item.title: Perth homeowner thought agents were selling his home; later found out they were the buyers
item.description: A Perth homeowner says he was unaware that the real estate agents hired to sell his home also owned the company that bought it for $705,000. Chao “Jack” Wu later discovered the connection through corporate records and said he believed the property was undersold. A retrospective valuation put its value at $800,000, while the agents disputed the valuation and denied wrongdoing. Western Australia’s Consumer Protection issued a formal warning to the agency over an alleged conflict of interest.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: Alix Earle’s family bought a $2.25M New Jersey mansion in 2013; now worth $4.1M, it stars on Netflix
item.description: Alix Earle, the popular figure on social media, is about to unveil her new reality series on Netflix, prominently featuring her family's lavish mansion in New Jersey. This property, which her father purchased for $2.25 million back in 2013, has soared in value to an impressive $4.1 million. Audiences can anticipate an engaging exploration of family interactions set within the comfort of their home.

item.title: In 1962, NASA exploded 22,900 gallons of water 65 miles above Earth to study the atmosphere
item.description: NASA explored biological life-support systems for extended space travel decades ago. Researchers examined recycling resources and using living organisms to sustain astronauts. Plants and microorganisms could process waste and provide essential resources for missions. This early work laid the groundwork for future lunar and Martian settlements. Sustainable living beyond Earth remains a significant scientific and engineering challenge.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Zebra mussel DNA found in Utah’s Colorado River for first time, raising alarm
item.description: For the first time, Zebra mussel DNA has been found in Utah's Colorado River, raising alarms among wildlife officials. This finding follows a serious infestation documented near Loma, Colorado, in 2025. Concern is mounting over the potential harm this invasive species could cause to local ecosystems and infrastructure. Boaters are strongly encouraged to clean, drain, and dry their watercraft to avert further spread.

item.title: Scientists found that DNA once dismissed as "junk" helps chromosomes find their partners
item.description: Repetitive DNA near chromosome centers forms a unique barcode for partner recognition. This barcode guides chromosomes to their correct partners during egg cell development. When this DNA barcode is disrupted, chromosomes pair incorrectly or fail to pair. A quality-control system eliminates eggs with such errors before they mature. This discovery revives an old idea about "junk" DNA's role in reproduction.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Scientists found evolutionary highways in animal genomes dating back 600 million years
item.description: By examining thousands of genomes along with fragments of ancient chromosomes, researchers uncovered the intricate journey of animal evolution. Their findings highlight how chromosomes merged and changed over epochs, with some species retaining ancestral structures while others underwent significant reorganization. Notably, the fusion of chromosomes peaked approximately 550 million years ago, leaving lasting impacts on the genetic frameworks of various animal lineages.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: MIT scientists watched electrons rebuild in a quantum material like ice crystals
item.description: Researchers at MIT have successfully captured two distinct recoveries of electron order in a quantum material. One phase emerged in a smooth fashion, while the other manifested in fragmented clusters. This work resolves ongoing discussions around the formation of specific electronic phases. Utilizing laser pulses, the team disrupted the material and studied its recovery, paving the way for innovative methods to explore competing quantum orders in real time.

item.title: Biological parents reveal why they asked surrogate to abort baby with serious heart condition
item.description: Nausheen Gilkar and Omar Ahmed revealed in court why they asked surrogate McKenna West to terminate their pregnancy after their unborn baby was diagnosed with hypoplastic left heart syndrome. West refused and later sought custody of newborn Rumi, who remains critically ill after undergoing the Norwood procedure. A Dallas judge has extended a temporary restraining order while considering the custody dispute.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Council orders Turkish firm to tear down holiday homes after trees cut down in ancient woodland
item.description: A mystery Turkish firm has been ordered by a council to tear down holiday homes built without planning permission in a 500-year-old English woodland. The company bought the 33-acre Jacobs Farm in Silsden for £1.05 million two years ago. A planning inspector rejected its appeal and ordered 100 trees to be planted to replace those lost during the unauthorised works.

item.title: Who was Andreethegirl? TikToker Andree Greig Baudoin dies at 39 after cancer battle
item.description: Andree Greig Baudoin, beloved TikToker known as Andreethegirl, tragically passed away at the age of thirty-nine. She candidly shared her battle with metastatic cancer on her platform, offering insights into her struggles and triumphs. In her final video, she expressed heartfelt gratitude to her followers, encouraging everyone to treasure their health and the simple joys of life.
